subject: Post-call: telemetry handling checklist & next actions
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medbridge.com>
Cc: ops@medbridge.com
Date: 2028-07-14T15:03:00Z
Subject: Post-call: telemetry handling checklist & next actions

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + concrete next steps so your security and platform teams have something to act on.

Summary of ask (as I understood it):
- MedBridge captures request/response traces from client-side apps into your ingestion pipeline. You need guidance on what to keep in logs, what to mask/obfuscate, and recommended retention windows to meet your privacy posture.
- Priority items: remove PII from request/response bodies, ensure headers/trace IDs are not usable to re-identify users, and qualify options for EU/US residency.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Ingest-time scrubbing: apply regex/field-level rules to remove email/SSN/national IDs before storage.
2) Header handling: hash trace IDs with a per-environment salt (one-way) so traces can be correlated internally but not linked to external identifiers.
3) KV cache/prefixes: redact full request prefixes containing user content; keep length-limited placeholders for debugging.
4) Retention: 30 days by default for debug logs; 90 days with admin approval for incident investigations. We can support shorter/longer windows per repo.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight telemetry checklist and a redaction matrix that maps common header/payload fields to suggested actions.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm whether your ingestion pipeline currently performs regex scrubbing or relies on downstream processors (ops@medbridge.com).
- Security: share any mandatory retention/residency rules (e.g., HIPAA constraints) and a list of fields that must be purged immediately after ingest.
- Redwood: we can put together a demo showing our request/response masking flow and a sample export with hashed trace IDs.

When's best for a short follow-up demo? I can do Tue or Thu morning PT next week.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Date: 2028-07-14T18:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: telemetry handling checklist & next actions

Thanks Alex — that summary is helpful. A few clarifying points from the security/ops side:

- Our ingestion pipeline (Kafka -> Flink -> S3) does minimal scrubbing today; most of the redaction work is done downstream in batch jobs. We want to push more to upstream to reduce exposure.
- HIPAA applies to certain product flows; for those we need logs retained no more than 14 days unless explicitly escalated for an incident. Non-PHI logs can stay 90 days.
- Trace IDs: we prefer reversible tokens for internal debugging but need a strong access control model. If irreversible hashing is the default, we'd need an audit path for any incident where re-identification is required.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can your masking step be done at the edge (before it hits our Kafka topic)?
2) Can you support per-stream retention policies and per-stream residency (we have EU customers where logs must remain in eu-central-1)?
3) For trace IDs, can you provide both hashed and reversible (KMS-wrapped) variants depending on the stream's sensitivity?

ops@medbridge.com — please confirm whether pushing scrubbing to the edge is feasible. Security — any immediate red lines we should be aware of before a demo?

Laura Chen
Director, Platform Security
MedBridge Health

Laura — good questions, answers below to align expectations before a demo. Marissa/Sean: tagging you for pricing/procurement and SLA questions.

Answers:
1) Edge scrubbing: yes — we can deploy a lightweight scrubbing proxy (sidecar or ingestion gateway) that applies field-level filters and header rules before events hit Kafka. That reduces blast radius.
2) Per-stream retention & residency: supported. We can route sensitive streams to EU-resident storage and keep separate retention policies per topic. We'll need to map your topics to sensitivity tiers.
3) Trace IDs: flexible. Default recommendation is to hash with a per-environment salt (irreversible). For streams where you need reversible mapping, we can store an encrypted mapping in a KMS-backed store with strict audit logs and RBAC. That option increases attack surface and cost — we flag it for security review.

Demo proposal: 20-minute walk-through focusing on:
- Edge scrubbing proxy and how it integrates with Kafka topics
- Header/trace ID handling modes (hashed vs KMS-wrapped)
- Retention/residency policies per stream
- Incident workflow: how to request a temporary re-identification (audit trail + approvals)

Available slots: Tue 2028-07-19 09:00 PT, Thu 2028-07-21 10:30 PT. Which works for your team?

Also attached a matrix that maps typical headers and payload fields to suggested actions (keep, mask, hash, drop).

Cheers —
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
